strengths: Presents a single-forward pass framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting stylization that works from unposed multi-view inputs (or a single view) without requiring per-scene test-time optimization.

Well-motivated architecture that disentangles geometry and appearance: the geometric backbone is preserved to retain structure, while style features are injected via global cross-attention to predict spherical harmonics color coefficients.
Proposes an intuitive voxel-based 3D style loss that computes feature distribution statistics in 3D voxel space rather than independent 2D views, effectively improving cross-view consistency.
Systematic ablations evaluating style-content coupling mechanisms (frame-only, hybrid, global-only) and style loss designs (image-level, scene-level, 3D voxel-level).
Extensive qualitative demonstrations showcasing zero-shot generalization across held-out categories (CO3D) and complex real-world scenes (Tanks and Temples).
weaknesses: Evaluation lacks a user study: assessing style transfer aesthetics and content preservation is inherently subjective, and a perceptual user study is standard practice in style transfer literature.

Limited baselines: comparisons are only conducted against per-scene optimization methods (StyleRF and StyleGS). A straightforward feed-forward baseline (e.g., applying 2D style transfer followed by feed-forward 3DGS like AnySplat) is not evaluated.

Details on the voxelized 3D style loss (Eq. 6 and Algorithm 3) are somewhat underspecified; specifically, how empty voxels/background sparsity are handled when calculating mean and standard deviation of voxel features, which could heavily bias the statistics.
Performance deteriorates when scaling to larger batch sizes (>32 views), exhibiting edge artifacts due to Gaussian instability and distribution shift from training.
Minor presentation flaws, such as incomplete sentences ('Our codes will be available at' in the abstract/introduction) and recurring typos in figure captions ('imamge' in Figures 8 and 14).

strengths: Presents an end-to-end feed-forward framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting stylization from unposed multi-view or single-view images, bypassing costly per-scene optimization and camera pose estimation.

The two-pathway Transformer architecture cleanly decouples geometry prediction (preserving self-attention priors from VGGT) from appearance/style transfer (conditioned via global cross-attention), preventing geometric collapse during stylization.

Introduces an innovative voxel-based 3D style loss that aligns 3D feature distribution statistics with 2D style statistics, which effectively enhances view consistency compared to standard 2D image-level style losses.

Provides extensive qualitative results across multiple datasets (CO3D, Tanks and Temples, DL3DV-10K) and various art styles, demonstrating good zero-shot generalization to unseen categories and scenes.
weaknesses: Discrepancy in the description of the 3D style loss: The text in Section 3.4 states that multi-view features are accumulated and fused into a single voxel volume $G_b^l$ prior to computing mean and standard deviation. However, Algorithm 3 in the Appendix places the voxelization, mean/std calculation, and loss accumulation inside the view loop `for s = 1 to S do`, which suggests per-view voxelization rather than joint multi-view feature fusion. This inconsistency should be clarified.

Evaluation scope and missing user studies: Quantitative evaluation on Tanks and Temples is restricted to only four scenes. Furthermore, because style transfer is fundamentally subjective and involves trade-offs between style stylization strength and geometry/content fidelity, a perceptual user study comparing against the baselines is missing.

Limited baseline landscape: The evaluation only compares against per-scene optimization methods (StyleRF, StyleGS). A discussion or baseline comparing a naive feed-forward 2D style transfer followed by feed-forward 3D reconstruction (e.g., AdaIN + AnySplat) would help quantify the direct benefits of joint 3D stylization.

Discrepancy regarding scalability claims: While the abstract and introduction emphasize scalability 'from a single to hundreds of views', Section 4.1 acknowledges that visual quality degrades beyond 32 views (with noticeable artifacts at 64 views). The scalability claims should be tempered to match the empirical findings.

strengths: Timely and ambitious problem setting: Tackling feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting stylization directly from unposed multi-view inputs without per-scene optimization is an appealing direction.

Well-motivated architecture: Decoupling geometric reasoning (retained in the self-attention VGGT backbone) from style conditioning (via cross-attention) provides a principled structural framework for 3D style transfer.

Voxel-based style loss formulation: Extending AdaIN-style feature statistics into 3D voxel space offers a sound conceptual direction to enforce view-consistent stylization beyond 2D frame-level losses.
weaknesses: Inconsistency in core method description: In Section 3.4, the text and Eq. (6) state that multi-view features are accumulated and fused into a single 3D discretized volume before computing voxel-level style statistics. However, Algorithm 3 lines 4–9 explicitly iterate over each view index s, voxelize Fr(k)[s] per-view, and compute MeanStd(V) inside the loop, directly contradicting the multi-view feature fusion narrative.

Overstated scalability claims: The paper claims scalability from a single view to 'hundreds of views' in the Abstract and Section 1. However, Section 4.1 and Figure 4 explicitly acknowledge that visual quality degrades once batch sizes exceed 32 views and produces noticeable structural and edge artifacts at 64 views.

Absence of human perceptual evaluation: Because cross-view consistency metrics (LPIPS, RMSE) heavily favor smooth or blurry textures, consistency metrics alone cannot measure stylization quality. The evaluation lacks user studies or comprehensive perceptual benchmarks assessing style fidelity, content preservation, and overall aesthetic preference.

Limited stylization fidelity and texture expressiveness: Qualitative results (Figure 5 and Appendix Figures 7–16) show that the transferred style often manifests as low-contrast color tinting or smooth washes, lacking the crisp brushstrokes, local structures, and rich artistic texture transfers characteristic of competitive neural style transfer methods.

Limited baseline selection: Comparisons are restricted to two older per-scene optimization methods (StyleRF and StyleGS). Comparison against other recent feed-forward multi-view reconstruction and stylization baselines or 2D diffusion-based lifting methods is missing.

Clarity and presentation defects: The abstract terminates abruptly with an unfinished sentence ('Our codes will be available at '), and multiple typographic errors persist in figure captions (e.g., 'imamge' in Figures 8 and 14, nested citations like '(Knapitsch et al. (2017a))').

strengths: Compelling and practical task: The paper addresses zero-shot, feed-forward 3D stylization with 3D Gaussian Splatting from unposed multi-view images without requiring per-scene optimization or camera calibration, achieving extremely fast inference (~0.05s).

Principled architectural and objective design: The disentangled dual-pathway Transformer architecture effectively isolates geometric reasoning from aesthetic transfer. Furthermore, the proposed 3D voxel-based AdaIN style loss innovatively aggregates multi-view features into a 3D volume before computing statistical moments, directly enforcing view-consistent stylization.

Thorough ablation study: The experiments validate key design choices, including the comparison between frame-level, global-level, and hybrid cross-attention, as well as image-level, scene-level, and 3D voxel-level style losses.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: Stylos is benchmarked on both object-centric (CO3D) and complex scene datasets (Tanks & Temples, DL3DV) against recent per-scene optimization (G-Style, SGSST, StylizedGS) and feed-forward (Styl3R) methods across diverse metrics (view consistency, ArtScore, ArtFID, CFSD, efficiency).

Good versatility and controllability: The method demonstrates successful style interpolation (multi-style blending) and continuous adjustment of stylization strength via post-inference latent blending without retraining.
weaknesses: Appearance-only stylization: Stylos only transfers appearance/color by predicting spherical harmonic coefficients while freezing geometry. It cannot modify underlying primitive geometry to reflect geometric style features (e.g., cubist shape deformations or stylized geometric abstractions).

Resolution and detail limits: The model operates at a fixed resolution (448x448) constrained by the underlying feed-forward Transformer backbone, leading to occasional blurriness or loss of high-frequency geometry (e.g., thin structures, foliage) compared to native full-resolution per-scene optimization methods.

Backbone scalability limitations: Performance and geometric stability degrade when scaling beyond 32–64 views, inherited from the underlying VGGT backbone characteristics as acknowledged in the limitations.
Minor presentation typos: Table 5 and Table 6 captions contain minor typos ('sylization quality metrics', 'HistoGAN loos').

strengths: Addresses an important and practical problem by replacing slow, per-scene optimization in 3D scene stylization with an efficient, feed-forward single-pass 3D Gaussian Splatting framework operating on unposed multi-view inputs.

Well-motivated architecture that decouples geometry estimation from style transfer: keeping geometric reasoning intact in a frozen/pre-trained backbone while injecting style attributes through a dedicated Style Aggregator via global cross-attention.
Introduces an innovative voxel-based 3D style loss that lifts 2D style feature statistics into a shared 3D voxel space, improving multi-view stylistic consistency.

Extensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (CO3D, DL3DV-10K, Tanks & Temples) with comparisons against optimization-based 3DGS baselines and contemporaneous feed-forward models, complemented by comprehensive ablation studies and honest discussions of failure cases in the appendix.
weaknesses: The quantitative margin between the proposed 3D voxel loss (Eq. 5) and the 2D scene-level style loss (Eq. 4) in Table 2 is relatively modest (e.g., Short-range RMSE 0.034 vs. 0.036, Long-range LPIPS 0.153 vs. 0.156, ArtScore 9.15 vs. 9.12), making it somewhat ambiguous whether the computational overhead of 3D differentiable unprojection and voxel fusion is essential compared to simpler multi-view feature concatenation.

The core pipeline heavily inherits architectural components and training recipes from VGGT and AnySplat, meaning the structural contributions mainly lie in adapting these architectures with cross-attention and voxel-level AdaIN losses.

Stylization performance degrades when input views exceed ~32 frames (as acknowledged in Section 4.1 and Figure 4) due to memory constraints and error accumulation from the underlying VGGT backbone, which limits scalability to larger-scale multi-view capture setups.

While inference is real-time (0.05s), per-scene optimization baselines (such as G-Style) still achieve superior style fidelity and lower FID/ArtFID in several benchmarks (e.g., Tables 4, 5, and 6), representing an expected but important quality-speed trade-off.

strengths: Efficient feed-forward pipeline: Stylos enables instant 3D stylization from unposed multi-view images in a single forward pass (~0.05s on a modern GPU), removing the need for both pre-computed camera poses and time-consuming per-scene/per-style optimization required by existing 3DGS stylization methods.

Clean disentanglement design: Decoupling geometric feature reasoning (preserving the self-attention structure of the VGGT backbone) from appearance/color conditioning (via the cross-attention Style Aggregator) prevents style conditioning from corrupting underlying 3D geometry.

3D Voxel-space style loss: Extending AdaIN-style feature statistics matching to a differentiable voxel grid effectively aggregates multi-view information, providing a better 3D-consistent supervisory signal during Stage 2 fine-tuning compared to purely 2D image-level or concatenated scene-level losses.

Controllability and interpolability: The framework demonstrates smooth latent interpolation between different styles and between original content and stylized appearance without requiring architectural modifications or re-training.
weaknesses: Limited stylization expressiveness and brushstroke fidelity: Because the stylization relies primarily on VGG feature statistics (mean and standard deviation) matching and a moderate resolution (448x448), the transferred results predominantly exhibit global color shifts and palette matching rather than intricate painterly strokes, structural stylization, or high-frequency artistic textures. In many qualitative examples (e.g., Figures 3, 5, 8–10), the stylized surfaces appear somewhat blurry or flatly color-mapped.

Discrepancy in scalability claims: The paper claims scalability to 'hundreds of views' in the abstract and introduction, yet Section 4.1 acknowledges a noticeable drop in visual quality once the view count exceeds 32 views, with prominent edge and reconstruction artifacts at 64 views due to backbone instability.

Incomplete and mixed comparative evaluation against feed-forward baselines: The comparison with Styl3R (the most directly comparable feed-forward baseline) lacks quantitative results on the 'Train' scene in Tables 3 and 4 without clear justification. Furthermore, in Tables 5 and 6, per-scene optimization methods like G-Style frequently achieve superior FID, LPIPS, and CFSD scores, highlighting the remaining visual fidelity gap between the proposed feed-forward approach and optimization-based methods.

Moderate technical novelty: The core system heavily integrates existing building blocks—specifically VGGT for pose/geometry estimation, AnySplat for unprojection/voxelization, and classical AdaIN-style moments matching adapted to voxel grids. While well integrated, the conceptual novelty of the underlying components is somewhat incremental.
